sections.summary: Remote work expanded after the pandemic and survey methods vary.
Hybrid and fully remote arrangements are often conflated in public debate.
The evidence base includes randomized field experiments and working-paper syntheses.
The Nature Trip.com trial found hybrid work reduced quit rates by roughly one-third without damaging performance.
Stanford SIEPR work distinguishes hybrid schedules from fully remote work and cautions that outcomes vary by task and arrangement.
Recommendation: treat hybrid work as a retention tool with performance monitoring, not as proof of universal productivity gains.
Appendix survey tables list demographic details and survey harmonization notes.
